mainTopic: Dividing shared property that cannot be split well: the rule of גוד או אגוד, and sharing a slave by days
overview: This amud first finishes the case of a field with water on two sides, which is split diagonally so each brother touches both. Then it returns to the משנה about a hall (טרקלין) too small to split. רב יהודה says a partner can force a buyout with גוד או אגוד; רב נחמן says he cannot. רבא challenges רב נחמן with brothers who inherit a slave, and רב נחמן answers that they share the slave's days. The גמרא then objects to רב יהודה from a משנה about a half-slave. There the court forces the master to free him only because he could not otherwise marry and have children. The גמרא answers that this case is different: the slave can buy his master's half, but he cannot sell himself, so גוד או אגוד could not work there anyway. Finally the גמרא begins a new proof about two brothers, one rich and one poor, who inherit a bathhouse and an olive press. That proof continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A field between a channel and a river is split diagonally
steps.stepSummary: If a field has a water channel on one side and a river on the other, the brothers split it diagonally.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there is a channel on one side and a river on the other side, they divide the field diagonally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes an earlier case about splitting a field between two brothers. Water is on two sides, so the field is cut on a diagonal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A straight cut would give one brother all the river side and the other all the channel side. A diagonal cut gives each brother some land touching both water sources. That way the split is fair.

phrases.english: On one side, a water channel
and on the other side, a river
they divide it diagonally.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד גִּיסָא נִגְרָא וְחַד גִּיסָא נַהֲרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the discussion from the previous daf about how to split a field.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A field between a channel and a river is divided diagonally so each heir gets access to both.

steps.title: What if the hall is too small to split?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a hall and asks what happens when there is not enough room for each partner.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: "And not a hall, etc." If there is not enough for this one and for that one, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה. The משנה says a hall is not split unless each side gets a usable share. Now the גמרא asks what to do when it is too small, and one partner wants out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה tells us we do not split it. It does not tell us how a partner can end the partnership. The question is whether he is stuck forever, or whether there is another way out.

keyTerms.meaning: A hall or large reception room
Enough for this one and enough for that one, meaning a usable share for each

phrases.english: "And not the hall, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: a hall is not divided unless each side would get enough to use.

phrases.english: If there is not enough for this one
and for that one, what is the law?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין בָּהֶן כְּדַי לָזֶה וּכְדֵי לָזֶה, מַהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the field case and returns to a new line in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: When shared property is too small to divide, can a partner force an end to the partnership?

steps.title: רב יהודה: a partner can force a buyout
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says the rule of גוד או אגוד applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: There is a law of "You set a price, or I will set a price."
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question. He says one partner can force the other into a buyout.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under גוד או אגוד, one partner says: "Name a price. Either you buy my half at that price, or I buy yours." Neither side wants to name an unfair price, because it might be used against him. This lets a partner leave property that cannot be split.

keyTerms.meaning: "You set a price, or I will set a price": a forced buyout between partners

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
There is a law of "You set a price, or I will set a price."
phrases.notes: Literally "you pull or I pull." It means one partner names a price, and that price decides who buys out whom.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר: אִית דִּינָא דְּגוּד אוֹ אֶגּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first answer to the question in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. One partner can force a buyout with גוד או אגוד.

steps.title: רב נחמן: no forced buyout
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן disagrees and says there is no rule of גוד או אגוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: There is no law of "You set a price, or I will set a price."
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן gives the opposite answer. A partner cannot force a buyout, so the partnership continues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, the partners cannot be made to sell or buy. They must keep sharing the property. That raises a practical question: how do they share something that cannot be split? The next step presses on exactly that.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
There is no law of "You set a price, or I will set a price."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר: לֵית דִּינָא דְּגוּד אוֹ אֶגּוּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב יהודה in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No. A partner cannot force a buyout; they keep sharing.

steps.title: רבא asks about brothers who inherit a slave and an animal
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן how a בכור and a regular brother would split a slave and a non-kosher animal without גוד או אגוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: According to you, who say there is no law of "You set a price, or I will set a price," what do they do if a firstborn and a regular son inherit a slave and a non-kosher animal from their father?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא challenges רב נחמן with a case of things that cannot be split. Without a forced buyout, how do the brothers divide them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave or a living animal cannot be cut into pieces. It is even harder here, because the בכור gets a double share, so the split is two-thirds and one-third, not half and half. רבא is pushing רב נחמן to show how his view works in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: Firstborn son, who inherits a double share

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Naḥman:
According to you, who say
there is no law of "You set a price, or I will set a price,"
a firstborn and a regular son
whose father left them
a slave and a non-kosher animal,
how do they do it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: לְדִידָךְ דְּאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב נחמן's view from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's view that there is no גוד או אגוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Some things cannot be physically split, especially in unequal shares. Without a forced buyout, there seems to be no way to divide them.

steps.title: רב נחמן: share by days
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that they split the slave's work by time: one day for the regular brother, two days for the בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I say, he works for this one one day, and for that one two days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא. They share the slave by dividing his time, not by forcing a sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you cannot split the thing, you can split the time. The regular brother gets one day and the בכור gets two, which matches his double share. So רב נחמן's view still works without גוד או אגוד.

phrases.english: He said to him: I say:
he works for this one one day,
and for that one two days.
phrases.notes: The two days go to the בכור, since he gets a double share.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ, שֶׁאֲנִי אוֹמֵר: עוֹבֵד לָזֶה יוֹם אֶחָד
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical solution: dividing by time instead of by object
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without a forced buyout, a slave could not be divided at all.
steps.terutzMaskana: The slave's work is divided by days, in proportion to each brother's share.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה lets a partner force a buyout (גוד או אגוד). רב נחמן does not; instead the partners share by time, for example by giving the slave's days in proportion.

steps.title: An objection begins: the half-slave who serves by days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: a man who is half slave and half free serves his master one day and himself one day, according to בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: One who is half slave and half free works for his master one day and for himself one day. These are the words of בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts an objection against רב יהודה's rule of גוד או אגוד. Right now it is only quoting the opening of a משנה about a half-slave; the challenge becomes clear when the quote ends in step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל's first ruling splits the slave's days, just like רב נחמן's solution. The גמרא quotes the whole משנה because its ending, where the master is forced to free the slave only for a special reason, will be used against רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: They objected, bringing a challenge from an earlier source

steps.confusionAlert: This objection is aimed at רב יהודה, not at רב נחמן's day-splitting. The point comes at the end of the משנה (step 9): the court forces a buyout only because of having children, so normally there is no forced buyout.

phrases.english: They objected:
One who is half slave
and half free –
works for his master one day,
and for himself one day;
these are the words of Beit Hillel.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי: מִי שֶׁחֶצְיוֹ עֶבֶד וְחֶצְיוֹ בֶּן חוֹרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts an objection against רב יהודה's rule of גוד או אגוד from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's view that there is a general rule of גוד או אגוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Begins quoting a משנה whose final ruling forces the master to free the slave only for the special reason of having children. That suggests there is no general forced buyout. The point is made in step 9.

steps.title: בית שמאי: splitting his days leaves him unable to marry
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי argue that splitting the days helps the master but hurts the half-slave, who cannot marry anyone, and the world was made for having children.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: You have fixed things for his master, but you have not fixed things for him. He cannot marry a maidservant, and he cannot marry a free woman. Should he just stay unmarried? But the world was created only for having children, as it says: "He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the source with בית שמאי's protest. They argue that splitting the days does not solve this man's problem. The rest of their argument comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His free half cannot marry a שפחה, and his slave half cannot marry a free Jewish woman. So the day-split leaves him unable to marry at all, which goes against the purpose of creation, פריה ורביה. This special reason is what will justify forcing the master in step 9. That is the basis of the challenge to רב יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: Should he stay idle, that is, not marry?
Having children (the מצוה to be fruitful and multiply)

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
You have fixed things for his master;
for himself you have not fixed things!
To marry a maidservant – he cannot,
to marry a free woman – he cannot;
Should he stay idle?!
But was the world not created
only for having children,
as it is said:
"He did not create it to be empty; He formed it to be lived in"!

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: תִּקַּנְתֶּם אֶת רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the source quoted in step 7 and makes its challenging point.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's view that there is a general rule of גוד או אגוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: בית שמאי give a special reason, having children, for ending this partnership. Because the court needs such a reason to force the master, it seems a partner cannot normally force a buyout.
steps.whyThisMatters: This special reason, having children, is what makes the משנה look like proof that there is no general rule of גוד או אגוד, against רב יהודה.

steps.title: The court forces the master to free the half-slave, and בית הלל agree
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי finish their ruling: the court forces the master to free the slave, and the slave writes a שטר owing half his value. בית הלל change their view to agree. This finishes the challenge: forcing is needed only because of having children, which suggests there is no general rule of גוד או אגוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, we force his master to make him a free man, and he writes a document for half his value. And בית הלל went back and ruled like בית שמאי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה. בית שמאי give their solution, and בית הלל switch to agree with them. This completes the challenge that began in steps 7-8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The court only forces the master to give up his half because the slave cannot marry and have children. If גוד או אגוד were a general rule, we would not need that special reason, since either side could always force the partnership to end. So the משנה seems to show there is no such rule in normal cases.

keyTerms.meaning: We force; the court compels someone
A written document, here a document of debt
Half his value (the master's half of the slave)
And they went back, meaning they changed their opinion

steps.confusionAlert: The master does not lose his money. He loses his half of the slave, but the freed man owes him half his value through the שטר.

phrases.english: Rather, we force his master
phrases.notes: This is still בית שמאי talking, giving their fix after the problem in step 8.

phrases.english: and make him a free man,
and write a document for half his value.
phrases.notes: The freed man now owes his old master the value of the half that was freed.

phrases.english: And בית הלל went back
to rule like the words of בית שמאי!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְחָזְרוּ בֵּית הִלֵּל לְהוֹרוֹת כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the משנה quote begun in steps 7-8 and makes the challenge complete.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's view that there is a general rule of גוד או אגוד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one partner could always force the other to buy or sell, the court would not need the special reason of having children to force the master. Since it needs that reason, there seems to be no general rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The court forces the master to free the half-slave, who writes a debt for half his value. בית הלל accept this.

steps.title: The half-slave case is different: he can buy but cannot sell
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the half-slave case is special. The slave can say "I will take" (אגוד), but he cannot offer "you take" (גוד), because he cannot sell himself. So the rule cannot work here, and the court needed the special reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different here, because "I will take" is possible, but "you take" is not possible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יהודה's rule of גוד או אגוד. It says the half-slave case is unusual, so it proves nothing about normal partners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: גוד או אגוד only works when each side can either buy or sell. The half-slave can buy his master's half, but he cannot sell his free half to his master, because a free Jew cannot sell himself as a full slave. Since only one direction works, the court needed the reason of having children to force the master. In normal partnerships, both directions work, so the rule still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different here; this case is special
"I will take": I set a price and buy your share
"You take": you set a price and buy my share
There is not; it is not possible

steps.whatToRemember: גוד או אגוד needs both choices to be possible. In the half-slave case only one choice exists, so this משנה does not disprove the rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the rule depends on both partners being able to buy and sell. A case where one side cannot sell is not a test of the rule.

phrases.english: It is different here,
because "I will take" exists, but "you take" does not exist.
phrases.notes: He means the slave can buy his master's half, but he cannot sell himself to his master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by showing the half-slave case is a special exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (שאני הכא): the source is an unusual situation where the rule cannot work.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because the court needed a special reason to force the master, we might think there is no general rule of גוד או אגוד.
steps.terutzMaskana: The special reason was needed only because the slave cannot sell himself. Where both sides can buy and sell, גוד או אגוד can still apply.

steps.title: New proof: two brothers inherit a bathhouse and an olive press
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a new משנה. Two brothers, one poor and one rich, inherit a bathhouse and an olive press. If the father built them to earn money, the profit is shared. If he built them for himself, the rich brother can say something to the poor brother. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Two brothers, one poor and one rich, and their father left them a bathhouse and an olive press. If he made them for profit, the profit is shared. If he made them for himself, the rich brother can say to the poor brother:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new attempt to prove whether there is a rule of גוד או אגוד. This step only sets up the case; the rich brother's words come on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is about brothers who own something together but use it in different ways. A poor brother has little use for a private bathhouse or olive press. The question will be whether one brother can force the other to buy or sell, which tests גוד או אגוד.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear; the גמרא brings a source to prove a point
For profit; to charge other people for using it

steps.confusionAlert: The sentence stops in the middle. What the rich brother says comes on the next amud, so do not decide yet what this proof shows.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
Two brothers,
one poor and one rich,
and their father left them
a bathhouse and an olive press;
if he made them for profit,
phrases.notes: "He" is the father: he built them to rent out to other people.

phrases.english: the profit is shared equally;
if he made them for himself,
then the rich brother says to the poor brother:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the half-slave case is set aside, the גמרא brings a new source to test the question of גוד או אגוד.
steps.raayaObject: Whether there is a rule of גוד או אגוד (the argument between רב יהודה and רב נחמן)
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about two brothers, one poor and one rich, who inherit a bathhouse and an olive press
